question.text: While returning home from a movie theatre, Ahmed Bouchikhi was misidentified and killed by members of this Israeli intelligence agency in Operation Wrath of God.
question.clue: This agency undertook an extrajudicial operation which captured and led to the execution of Adolf Eichmann after he was discovered hiding in Argentina.

swap.leadin: The Balfour Declaration supported the creation of a "national home" for members of a certain religion, which became this country.
swap.text: Name this country that was invaded by five Arab nations shortly after its creation in 1948.
swap.clue: Operation Badr penetrated this country's defensive Bar-Lev Line during a 1973 conflict that included a battle in the "Valley of Tears" fought as part of an effort to recapture the Golan ("goh-LAHN") Heights from it.

question.text: This conflict saw Operation Kadesh, an Israeli invasion of the Sinai Peninsula in a combined effort with Britain and France go take the namesake waterway.
question.clue: This conflict was the center of discussions at the Protocol of Sevres after which Charles Keightley initiated Operation Musketeer.

swap.text: This Islamic political organization was suppressed during Mubarak's time in office, but formed the Freedom and Justice Party to contest elections after Mubarak's resignation.
swap.answerHtml: Muslim Brotherhood (accept The Society of the Muslim Brothers)
swap.clue: Its first meeting place was created in Ismailia by its founder Hassan al-Bannah ("HAH-sen al-buh-NAH").

question.text: The Tang's western expansion was halted at the Battle of Talas, where they were defeated by this empire. This empire's capital of Baghdad, which contained the House of Wisdom, was destroyed by the Mongols in 1258.
question.clue: Several of its rulers relied on the Barmakids to administer it, and the Buyids later conquered its capital, built by al-Mansur.

swap.text: In 106 CE, the Roman emperor Trajan annexed the Nabatean kingdom in order to protect a road which had linked Alexandria to this city, a center of steel production. It was the capital of the Umayyad Caliphate.
swap.clue: Saladin left Egypt to establish an Ayyubid sultanate at this city, which would be the site of his death.

question.leadin: Mohammed Abdel Latif fired eight shots at this leader during a speech in Alexandria, but all eight missed.
question.text: Identify this leader whose one-party system was called the Liberation Rally. He joined with Muhammad Naguib to form the Free Officers Movement and overthrow Farouk I, and established the United Arab Republic.
question.clue: This leader helped overthrow King Farouk I in 1952 before founding the United Arab Republic in 1958.

swap.leadin: This man was found with a gold-plated Browning Hi-Power pistol, referencing his son's Khamis Brigade, at the time of his capture.
swap.text: Name this leader from Sirte, who came to power by overthrowing his country's King Idris. In 2003, this leader accepted responsibility for the Lockerbie bombing.
swap.clue: This leader changed his country's flag to a pure green banner and set out his ideas in the Green Book.

question.leadin: Identify these countries whose chief executives experienced varying degrees of difficulty in March 2009.
question.text: This nation's president, Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, became publicly irate at the National Auditing Service when they attempted to remind him that he had still yet to return a three year-old $1 billion surplus to the treasury, and that interior minister Ali Kordan still only had a fake college degree.
question.clue: The first President of this country authored the memoir My Turn to Speak and faced exile after being falsely implicated in the death of Mohammad Beheshti.

swap.leadin: BONUS. Answer the following about 1967 per part.
swap.text: This conflict saw Israeli forces take the old city of Jerusalem.
swap.clue: This war was followed by the War of Attrition, and it began shortly after Gamal Abdul Nasser closed the Straits of Tiran.

question.text: On his way to the Holy Land, Richard conquered Cyprus, which he traded to the Knights Templar, who eventually ceded it to this leader of the Lusignan dynasty. This guy had previously been king of the Jerusalem crusader state.

swap.text: This dam on the Nile River was built during Nasser's rule. This dam created a lake named for Nasser.
swap.clue: In 1956 John Foster Dulles announced that the US was withdrawing funding, following the Soviets offering over one billion dollars in funding.

question.leadin: This man drew heavily from falsafa sources and the writings of Avicenna in a work translated into Latin by Dominicus Gundissalinus of Toledo called The Intentions of the Philosophers.
question.text: Identify this Arabic philosopher who wrote The Incoherence of the Philosophers.

swap.leadin: This kingdom reclaimed its capital from the Seljuk empire after the Battle of Didgori.
swap.text: Name this kingdom, that was ruled by the Bagrationi dynasty.
swap.clue: This kingdom reclaimed its capital from a Seljuk emirate by winning the Battle of Didgori under the leadership of its king David the Builder.

question.text: The UN brokered a cease-fire line denoted by this adjective in the Golan Heights after the Six-Day War. It was breached by Syrian troops during the Yom Kippur War.

swap.leadin: In November 1917, Pravda and Izvestia published an agreement signed by these two diplomats that was reprinted by the Manchester Guardian.
swap.text: Name these two diplomats who signed a secret treaty in 1916 that informed negotiations at San Remo. The Balfour Declaration was made regarding territory assigned to Britain under that treaty signed by these diplomats.
swap.answerHtml: Mark Sykes AND François Georges-Picot [accept Sykes–Picot Agreement; accept Sir Tatton Benvenuto Mark Sykes in place of “Mark Sykes”; accept François Marie Denis Georges-Picot in place of “François Georges-Picot”]

question.leadin: Thomas Friedman named a set of "rules" that describes the ethos of the Middle East after this city.
question.text: Name this Syrian city where 300 people were killed in 1981 by government security forces. A year later, thousands of citizens were brutally murdered in this city as part of the repression of an uprising by the Muslim Brotherhood.

swap.text: Until the late 1960s, the Binladin Group had the exclusive contract to renovate this holy site, a mosque that shares its name with a militant wing of the Fatah Party.
swap.answerHtml: Al-<u>Aqsa</u> Mosque [or Al-Masjid al-<u>Aqsa</u>; accept Al-<u>Aqsa</u> Martyrs’ Brigade or Kata’ib Shuhada al-<u>Aqsa</u> or Masjid <u>Bayt al-Maqdis</u>; prompt on “<u>Farthest</u> Mosque” or “Mosque of the <u>Holy City</u>”]
swap.clue: This place, which members of the Gush Emunim had planned on blowing up during the 1980s. This place is also where a visiting King Abdullah I was assassinated in 1951.

question.text: This golden-voiced friend of Muhammad was born into slavery as the son of Ethiopian princess captured during the Abyssinian attempt to destroy the Kaaba during the Year of the Elephant. He was later freed and became the first muezzin.
question.answerHtml: Bilal ibn Rabah [or Bilal al-Habashi; or Bilal ibn Riyah; prompt on “ibn Rabah” or “al- Habashi” or “ibn Riyah”]

swap.leadin: Name these 7th century battles that were fought by Muslims.
swap.text: To avenge Uthman's death, Aisha mustered a large force, which met a Ali's troops near Basra. This battle, which basically pitted Muslims against fellow Muslims, is named for a large desert mammal that was used during the battle.
swap.answerHtml: Battle of the Camel [ or Battle of Jamal; or Battle of Bassorah]
